title: Erdős Problem #1110: Representability by Sums of p^k q^l
description: For coprime p > q ≥ 2, when can integers be represented as sums of p^k q^l where no term divides another? The {2,3} case has all positive integers representable; other cases have infinitely many exceptions.

overview.historicalContext:
**Erdős Problem #1110: Representability**

This problem concerns representing integers as sums of 'smooth' numbers (products of small primes) with a non-divisibility constraint.

**Historical Development:**
- **1992:** Erdős posed his 'silly conjecture' about {2,3}
- **1996:** Erdős-Lewin proved the characterization theorem
- **2022:** Yu-Chen established density results and coprime infinitude
- **2025:** Yang-Zhao improved minimum summand bounds

**The 'Silly Conjecture':**
Erdős called his {2,3} conjecture 'silly' after Jansen and others found a simple inductive proof. Yet the general problem remains deep and partially open.
overview.problemStatement:
**Problem Statement (Partially OPEN)**

Let p > q ≥ 2 be coprime. An integer n is representable if it equals a sum of terms p^k q^l where no term divides another.

**Questions:**
1. If {p,q} ≠ {2,3}, what is the density of non-representable numbers?
2. Are there infinitely many coprime non-representable numbers?

**Key Results:**
- {2,3}: ALL positive integers are representable (simple induction)
- Other cases: Infinitely many non-representable (Erdős-Lewin)
- Density zero in many cases (Yu-Chen 2022)
- Infinitely many coprime non-representables for most (p,q) (Yu-Chen)
overview.text: For coprime p > q ≥ 2, when can integers be represented as sums of p^k q^l where no term divides another? The {2,3} case has all positive integers representable; other cases have infinitely many exceptions.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Formalization Approach**

1. **Definitions:** IsPowerForm, NoOneDividesAnother, IsRepresentable

2. **The {2,3} Case:** Axiomatize that all n ≥ 1 are representable

3. **Erdős-Lewin:** Axiomatize the characterization (finite exceptions ↔ {2,3})

4. **Yu-Chen Results:** Density zero and coprime infinitude conditions

5. **Minimum Summand Bounds:** f(n) ~ n/log n

6. **Concrete Example:** Prove 1 is representable constructively
prerequisites: Elementary number theory: coprimality, divisibility, prime factorization of integers
Additive combinatorics: representation functions, sumsets, and density of integer subsets
Asymptotic density and natural density of subsets of the natural numbers
Logarithmic estimates and growth rates of arithmetic functions
keyInsights: **The 'Silly Conjecture':** Erdős's {2,3} conjecture had a simple inductive proof
**Inductive Structure:** Even n uses doubled representations; odd n subtracts 3^k
**Density Zero:** Non-representables are sparse for large p or q > 3
**Coprime Infinitude:** Most (p,q) have infinitely many coprime exceptions
**Minimum Summand:** Representations can use summands > n/log n

conclusion.summary: Erdős Problem #1110 asks about representing integers as sums of p^k q^l with non-divisibility. The {2,3} case is completely solved (all positive integers representable), but general cases have infinitely many exceptions. Yu-Chen (2022) established density zero for large parameters and coprime infinitude for most (p,q). The minimum summand can be as large as n/log n.
conclusion.implications:
**Theoretical Significance**: **Implications**

1. **Additive Structure:** Reveals how 'smooth' numbers combine additively
**2. Density Theory:** Non-representables form a thin set in many cases
3. **Number-Theoretic Constraints:** Non-divisibility creates rich structure
4. **Algorithmic:** Inductive proof gives explicit constructions for {2,3}.
openQuestions: What is the exact density of non-representables for small p, q?
Can the minimum summand bound be improved beyond n/log n?
What happens at the critical boundary cases for Yu-Chen conditions?
Are there other base pairs with all integers representable?

crossReferences.title: Erdős Problem #246: Completeness of {a^k b^l : k, l ≥ 0}
crossReferences.relationship: Direct predecessor: Problem #246 asks whether {a^k b^l} is a complete sequence (every large integer a sum of distinct elements), proved by Birch (1959). Problem #1110 builds on this by imposing the non-divisibility constraint on the summands, making the representation question substantially harder.

crossReferences.title: Erdős Problem #845: Sums of 3-Smooth Numbers with Bounded Ratio
crossReferences.relationship: Closely related: Problem #845 studies sums of 3-smooth numbers (powers of 2 and 3) under a bounded ratio constraint b_t ≤ Cb_1. The {2,3} case of Problem #1110 (all positive integers representable) directly intersects this setting; both problems probe the additive richness of the set {2^k · 3^l}.

crossReferences.title: Erdős #123: d-Complete Sequences
crossReferences.relationship: Thematic sibling: Problem #123 asks whether {a^i · b^j · c^k} is d-complete for pairwise coprime a, b, c. Both problems concern representability by products of prime powers; Problem #1110 restricts to two bases and adds a non-divisibility condition, while Problem #123 allows three bases and asks for d-completeness.

crossReferences.title: Erdős Problem #124: Complete Sequences from Digit-Restricted Sums
crossReferences.relationship: Related completeness theme: Problem #124 studies completeness of sums of integers with restricted digit representations in given bases, directly related to the structural question of which integer systems allow complete additive representation — the overarching question of Problem #1110.

crossReferences.title: Erdős Problem #1107: Sums of r-Powerful Numbers
crossReferences.relationship: Parallel representation problem: Problem #1107 asks whether every sufficiently large integer is a sum of at most r+1 many r-powerful numbers. Both problems study structured additive representations of integers under multiplicative constraints on the summands, and share the density-theoretic perspective on exceptions.

references.title: d-Complete Sequences of Integers
references.venue: Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society
references.note: Proves the characterization theorem: for coprime p > q ≥ 2, the number of non-representable integers is finite if and only if {p,q} = {2,3}. Introduces the non-divisibility representability framework.

references.title: On Representations by Sums of p^a q^b
references.note: Establishes density-zero results for non-representable integers in many parameter regimes and proves infinitely many coprime non-representable integers exist for most (p,q) ≠ {2,3}.

references.title: Note on a Problem of Erdős
references.venue: Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society
references.note: Proves completeness of {a^k b^l} for coprime a, b (Problem #246), which is the precursor result to Problem #1110's representability question without the non-divisibility constraint.

references.title: Minimum Summand Bounds for p^k q^l Representations
references.note: Improves the Yu-Chen lower bounds on the minimum summand in representations, showing the minimum summand f(n) satisfies f(n) ~ n / log n asymptotically.

references.title: On a Problem in Additive Number Theory
references.venue: Journal of the London Mathematical Society
references.note: Early Erdős work on representation by structured multiplicative sets, providing the additive-combinatorics context for Problem #1110 and the related d-completeness questions.
